summary: Verified Phase 2A, 2B, 3A mobile-app changes and Phase 3A backend endpoint. All four targeted items pass. Backend endpoint /api/products/top-selling-by-category requires Bearer auth, returns a JSON array with at most 5 items per category, each containing name/category/sales_count/image_url/cost_per_100g, and is sorted by sales_count desc per category (rating fallback). Mobile home Popular Items renders exactly 6 compact horizontal cards with working horizontal scroll while page vertical scroll still works. After adding an item, cart-pill is placed just above the bottom nav (~14px gap). Cart 'Forgot something? Add more' carousel renders 10 horizontally-scrollable addon cards with images and Add buttons; tapping addon-add-{id} adds the product to the unified cart.
passed_tests: BACKEND 3A: GET /api/products/top-selling-by-category without token => 403; with invalid token => 401; with admin token => 200 JSON array (11 items) grouped Carb=5, Protein=5, Fat=1 (<=5 per category). All items have name/category/sales_count/image_url/cost_per_100g. Items within each category sorted by sales_count desc. (pytest: 5/5 passed)

MOBILE 2B Popular Items: data-testid='popular-add-*' count = 6 (exactly the spec maximum). Horizontal scroll container observed scrollWidth=1020 vs clientWidth=420. Vertical page scroll works (scrollHeight=1701 vs clientHeight=814).

MOBILE 2A Cart pill placement: after popular-add tap, [data-testid='cart-pill'] visible at bottom y=808 in a viewport of 880 (tab bar starts at y=822) - the pill now sits just above the bottom navigation bar, not mid-screen.

MOBILE 3A Cart Add-more: /mobile/cart renders 'FORGOT SOMETHING? ADD MORE' section with 10 addon cards ([data-testid^='addon-']) and 10 add buttons ([data-testid^='addon-add-']). Container is horizontally scrollable (scrollWidth=1408 vs clientWidth=388). Each addon card has a product image. Tapping addon-add-<id> successfully updates the unified cart (CartContext).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py top_selling_by_category: confirm the per-category cap is enforced server-side (observed max=5). If sales_count==0 across the board, current fallback to 'rating' is in effect (all items in response showed sales_count=0). Consider exposing 'is_fallback_by_rating' flag in the response so the client can adjust UI if needed.
frontend/app/(tabs)/home.tsx: popularProducts.slice(0,6) and the smaller card sizes (popularCard width:156, popularImg height:104) look fine; consider memoizing the FlatList items if the list grows.
